analysis_steps.goal: Fit geometric model to GRAVITY visibilities

method.value: Chi-squared fits of uniform disk (compact) plus 2D Gaussian (extended) with flux ratios interpolated at eight wavelengths from 2.0 to 2.45 um

evidence.quote: We then performed chi-squared fits to determine the sizes of the two components, and to determine the flux ratios as a linear interpolation between eight equally spaced wavelengths between 2.0 and 2.45 $\mu$m (R$\sim$40).

assumptions.value: constant component sizes with wavelength; concentric in most trials

evidence.quote: we assumed that the VLTI-compact and the VLTI-extended components have constant sizes over the wavelength range covered by the VLTI/GRAVITY observations.
We then performed chi-squared fits to determine the sizes of the two components, and to determine the flux ratios as a linear interpolation between eight equally spaced wavelengths

findings_qualitative.value: Emission from both FU Ori and FU Ori S at (sub)mm and NIR is dominated by structures inside ~10 au; small closure phases imply approximately face-on, centrally symmetric.

evidence.quote: We detected closure phases close to zero from FU Ori with VLTI/GRAVITY, which indicate the source is approximately centrally symmetric and therefore is likely viewed nearly face-on.

findings_qualitative.value: Tentative evidence for vertical dust settling in inner 10 au of FU Ori

evidence.quote: we tentatively detect evidence of vertical dust settling in the inner 10 au of the FU Ori disk
